title: Memorandum to dispensing pharmacies: early-refill thresholds, travel overrides and synchronization fills
content:
To pharmacies dispensing Linden Ridge prescriptions of the Prescriptions & Renewals line. The figures below are set per prescription class and govern when the next fill of a prescription falls due and which early fills a class allows.

| Class | Early-refill threshold (share of the previous fill's days' supply that must have elapsed) | Travel override allowed | Travel overrides per prescription in a rolling 12 months | Medication synchronization allowed | Largest synchronization short fill (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | 0 percent | no | 0 | no | 0 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | 75 percent | yes | 1 | yes | 29 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | 75 percent | yes | 1 | yes | 29 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 85 percent | no | 0 | no | 0 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 90 percent | no | 0 | no | 0 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | 80 percent | yes | 1 | no | 0 |

**Explanatory notes.**

1. The early-refill threshold is the percentage of the previous fill's days' supply that must have elapsed before the next fill. A threshold of 0 percent marks a class in which no refills exist — the Acute Short-Course Prescription.
2. A travel override is an early fill for travel that overrides the early-refill threshold; the class column says whether it is allowed at all, and the count column caps how many one prescription may receive in a rolling 12 months.
3. A synchronization short fill is the short alignment fill used when a prescription is enrolled in medication synchronization; a 0 in the last column means it is not available.
4. Only the Standard Maintenance Prescription and the Monitored Maintenance Prescription allow both a travel override and synchronization; the Specialty Medication Prescription allows a travel override but not synchronization; neither controlled class allows either.
